notes.html: TODO (answers Simon's struck [NOTE], checked against csf_final): (1) T1 (RedeemBeforeTimeout) is not needed by any of the five liveness lemmas (necessity runs, Sec. V-D), so it is presented as well-formedness. (2) The decreasing deadlines of Rmk. 2 are T2b (OutgoingTimesOutFirst); the claiming liveness stated after Rmk. 2 is T3 (IntermediaryMustClaim). (3) Correct: punishment liveness is not encoded; none of the nine restrictions of csf_final mentions Cheat or Punish.

Replace the struck description by: If an HTLC is redeemed and its channel times out, the redemption comes first. This is not a liveness assumption but a well-formedness condition on timeouts: with T1 removed, all five liveness lemmas of Sec. V-D are still proved.

restriction RedeemBeforeTimeout:
    "All ptr y #i #j.
        Redeemed(ptr, y) @ #i & TimedOut(ptr) @ #j ==> #i < #j"

Replace by: Lemma (ForwardTimeGap, formerly Restr. T2a). If both the incoming and the outgoing HTLC of a forwarding hop time out, and the forwarder was not compromised before its incoming timeout, then the outgoing one times out first. This is no longer assumed: it follows from Restr. T2b and OneTimeoutPerPtr, and Tamarin proves it (make verify).

lemma ForwardTimeGap [reuse]:
    "All P Prev Next ptrIn ptrOut y #f #j #k.
        HTLCForwarded(P, Prev, Next, ptrIn, ptrOut, y) @ #f
      & TimedOut(ptrOut) @ #j
      & TimedOut(ptrIn)  @ #k
      & not (Ex #c. LtkCompromised(P) @ #c & #c < #k)
     ==> #j < #k"

TODO (answers Simon's margin question): yes, in csf_final it is proven from T2b, so only T1, T2b and T3 remain as liveness restrictions.

Replace by: Restriction T2b (OutgoingTimesOutFirst). If the incoming HTLC of a forwarding hop times out and the forwarder was not compromised before, then its outgoing HTLC timed out earlier. This is the decreasing-deadline (CLTV-delta) invariant of Rmk. 2. Forwarders compromised before their incoming timeout are not constrained.

restriction OutgoingTimesOutFirst:
    "All P Prev Next ptrIn ptrOut y #f #k.
        HTLCForwarded(P, Prev, Next, ptrIn, ptrOut, y) @ #f
      & TimedOut(ptrIn) @ #k
      & not (Ex #c. LtkCompromised(P) @ #c & #c < #k)
     ==> Ex #m. TimedOut(ptrOut) @ #m & #m < #k"

Replace the struck description by: If a forwarder's outgoing HTLC is redeemed and its incoming HTLC times out, and the forwarder was not compromised before that timeout, then its incoming HTLC is redeemed too. This is the claiming liveness of Rmks. 1 and 2. It only constrains traces in which the incoming HTLC times out, which are the only traces in which the upstream party can be refunded (Refund_Requires_Timeout). By T1, the claim then comes before the timeout. As a restriction, T3 does not penalise a missing claim but removes every such trace, including traces in which the forwarder could not have claimed in time; lemmas proved under T3 say nothing about those runs.

restriction IntermediaryMustClaim:
    "All P Prev Next ptrIn ptrOut y #f #i #k.
        HTLCForwarded(P, Prev, Next, ptrIn, ptrOut, y) @ #f
      & Redeemed(ptrOut, y) @ #i
      & TimedOut(ptrIn)  @ #k
      & not (Ex #c. LtkCompromised(P) @ #c & #c < #k)
     ==> Ex #l. Redeemed(ptrIn, y) @ #l"

Replace both versions (V1, V2) by: Restr. T1 is a well-formedness condition on timeouts. Restr. T2b encodes the decreasing deadlines of Rmk. 2, and ForwardTimeGap (formerly T2a) is derived from it. Restr. T3 is the liveness assumption on which intermediary safety rests. The necessity runs of Sec. V-D remove one restriction at a time. Without T1, all five liveness lemmas (ForwardTimeGap, Timeout_Race_Blocked, Intermediary_Never_Loses_Under_Liveness, Intermediary_Never_Loses_Strong, Payment_Atomicity_Under_Liveness) are still proved. Without T2b, Timeout_Race_Blocked and both intermediary-safety lemmas are still proved. Without T3, Tamarin finds a trace with no compromised party in which an intermediary's outgoing HTLC is redeemed while its incoming one is refunded (Necessity_IMC_Honest_Intermediary_Loses): an honest intermediary loses money. The remaining checks give no result within 600 s, and we draw no conclusion from them. Under these restrictions we prove payment atomicity, intermediary safety, routing causality, invoice authentication and preimage secrecy (Sec. V-C), the timing results of Sec. V-D, and that a forwarder at positions 1 to 6 of a route can be bypassed only if some key was compromised (Secs. V-E and VI). The bypass theorem for any position of a single-offer payment (Sec. VI) is proved without T1, T2b and T3.

notes.anchor: Restriction Eq. EQ(a,b) is true iff.
notes.html:
Add after this paragraph: Restr. Eq (Equality) is one of six structural restrictions. Equality and Inequality turn the Eq and Neq action facts into constraints. OneChannelPerPtr and OneTimeoutPerPtr let a channel be opened at most once and time out at most once, and OneHTLCPerHashPerChannel lets an HTLC with a given payment hash be added at most once per channel. The sixth, OneResolutionPerHTLC, lets each HTLC be resolved (redeemed or refunded, action fact Old) at most once; it stands for a guarantee of the channel layer, which in our model does not carry HTLC outputs (Sec. IV-B).

restriction Equality:
    "All x y #i. Eq(x, y) @ #i ==> x = y"

restriction Inequality:
    "All x y #i. Neq(x, y) @ #i ==> not(x = y)"

notes.anchor: Splitting a model comes with limitations
notes.html:
Replace the two struck paragraphs by:

Our artifact consists of one main theory and five small auxiliary models. The main theory, lightning.spthy, contains both the payment-channel layer (Sec. V-A1) and multi-hop routing over routes of any length (Sec. V-A2), under a single Dolev-Yao adversary that can also compromise long-term keys. The auxiliary models, all in lightning_aux.spthy and each selected by a preprocessor flag, cover what the main theory leaves out: the PTLC countermeasure (-D=PTLC) and its HTLC baseline (-D=HTLC), a block-clock model of CLTV deadlines (-D=CLOCK), CLTV-delta arithmetic (-D=CLTV) and the early-timeout race (-D=TIMEOUT). Each auxiliary model is self-contained and is not composed with the main theory; Table I states what each run establishes.

Inside the main theory, the two layers share only the long-term keys and the channel topology: Lock_Funds_And_Open mints the persistent !ChannelConnect facts and the per-channel slot Mutex(ptr) that the routing rules use. HTLC state is not folded into the commitment transactions: StateA and StateB carry balances and revocation data but no HTLC outputs. That an HTLC is resolved (redeemed or refunded) at most once is imposed by Restr. OneResolutionPerHTLC rather than derived from the channel mechanics. A mechanized link between HTLC resolution and the channel layer, for example by refinement, is future work.
Replace by: As stated in Sec. IV-B, the main theory contains both layers, as two groups of rules that share only the long-term keys and the channel topology.

Replace "signed commitment" by "commitment": StateA and StateB hold the commitment <'commit', ptr, $A, $B, n, h(sA)> without its signature; signatures appear only in the pending mirrors and are checked in Revoke_Old_Secret.

Replace by: Lock_Funds_And_Open mints the two mirrors together with the persistent facts !ValidOnChain(ptr), !ChannelRecord(ptr, $A, $B) and !ChannelConnect (one per direction), and the per-channel slot Mutex(ptr), which the routing rules take and give back (Sec. V-A2).

TODO: checked; both listings match csf_final. Publish_Current_A hides the action facts PublishState($A, n), OnChainDelayedProduce($A, n), OnChainInstantProduce($B, n) behind "..."; Claim_Funds_A is verbatim. The duplicate full listings on p. 9 are struck.

Replace Punish_B by Punish_A: in csf_final, Punish_A consumes the OnChainCheat($A, $B, ...) and RevealedSecret($A, ...) facts produced by Publish_Revoked_A and yields AllFundsTo($B) (action Punish($B, $A, n_old)).

Replace by: Forward obligations travel as linear facts Route($Prev, $Me, ptrIn, y), and every added HTLC is also recorded in a persistent fact !RouteInfo. Once an HTLC is redeemed, the preimage travels back as Fulfilled(ptr, x). The slot Mutex(ptr), minted when the channel opens (Sec. V-A1), acts as a per-channel lock: it is consumed whenever an HTLC is added to the channel and given back when that HTLC is redeemed or refunded. Hence no two HTLCs are pending on the same channel at the same time, while the channel stays reusable for later payments.

Replace the listing by the csf_final rule (verbatim):

rule Forward_HTLC:
    [ Route($Prev, $Me, ptrIn, y),
      !ChannelConnect(ptrOut, $Me, $Next),
      Mutex(ptrOut),
      In(%vIn), In(%fee), In(%vOut) ]
    --[ HTLCForwarded($Me, $Prev, $Next, ptrIn, ptrOut, y),
        HTLCAdded(ptrOut, y),
        FeeCharged($Me, y, %fee),
        Eq(%vIn,  %vOut %+ %fee),
        Neq(ptrIn, ptrOut), Neq($Prev, $Me), Neq($Me, $Next) ]->
    [ IntermediaryPending($Me, $Prev, $Next, ptrIn, ptrOut, y, %vIn, %vOut, %fee),
      Route($Me, $Next, ptrOut, y),
      !RouteInfo($Me, $Next, ptrOut, y) ]

Replace by: Forward_HTLC consumes Route($Prev, $Me, ptrIn, y) and produces Route($Me, $Next, ptrOut, y). It advances the payment one hop, takes the slot Mutex(ptrOut) of the outgoing channel, and stores in IntermediaryPending everything the hop needs to settle or to be refunded later. $Next is any party with which $Me shares a channel, so routes are built hop by hop and have no fixed length; this single rule serves every forwarding hop of every route. The incoming amount, the fee and the outgoing amount are chosen by the environment and constrained only by Eq(%vIn, %vOut %+ %fee). The action HTLCForwarded($Me, $Prev, $Next, ptrIn, ptrOut, y) identifies the hop in our lemmas, HTLCAdded(ptrOut, y) feeds Restr. OneHTLCPerHashPerChannel, and FeeCharged records the fee the hop expects. The Neq facts make the forwarder distinct from both of its neighbours and the two channels distinct from each other.

Replace by: Receiver_Create_Invoice signs the tagged invoice <'invoice', $Receiver, $Sender, y> with y = h(~x), sends it with its signature, and keeps the preimage private in ReceiverInv. Sender_Offer_HTLC checks that signature before offering the first HTLC. Receiver_Fulfill_HTLC consumes the last Route fact, checks Eq(h(x), y), emits Redeemed(ptrIn, y) and passes the preimage upstream as Fulfilled(ptrIn, x). The preimage is never sent over the network, and the adversary never learns it (Preimage_Never_Known). Intermediary_Settle then consumes IntermediaryPending and Fulfilled(ptrOut, x), emits Fulfilled(ptrIn, x) one hop upstream and records FeeEarned when the intermediary collects its fee. Both rules give the slot Mutex(ptrIn) back. Sender_Settle finally consumes SenderPending and Fulfilled(ptrSF, x) and closes the payment with SenderSettled.

notes.anchor: The complementarity of claiming and refunding
notes.html: Replace by: Both refund rules also give the slot Mutex back. Timeouts are untimed channel events: Open_Timeout may fire at any point once the channel exists, at most once per channel (OneTimeoutPerPtr), and makes the pending HTLCs on that channel refundable. The interplay of claiming and refunding is pinned down by the three liveness restrictions of Sec. IV-A: RedeemBeforeTimeout forbids redeeming after the timeout, OutgoingTimesOutFirst encodes the decreasing deadlines of Rmk. 2, and IntermediaryMustClaim encodes the claiming liveness of Rmks. 1 and 2.

TODO: add at the end of Sec. V-A2, just before this heading:

Besides the Dolev-Yao network and key compromise (Compromise_Ltk), the adversary has one routing rule, used for the wormhole:

rule AttackerSkip:
    [ Fulfilled(ptrExit, x),
      !RouteInfo(ExitAtt, Next, ptrExit, y)[-,no_precomp],
      !RouteInfo(EntryAtt, Skipped, ptrSkip, y)[-,no_precomp],
      !Compromised(ExitAtt),
      !Compromised(EntryAtt) ]
    --[ FulfilledProduced(ptrSkip, x),
        Skipped(ptrSkip, x),   // annotation: marks a wormhole skip
        Eq(h(x), y) ]->
    [ Fulfilled(ptrSkip, x) ]

If two compromised parties, ExitAtt and EntryAtt, have each added an HTLC for the same payment hash y, on channels ptrExit and ptrSkip, then AttackerSkip takes the preimage released on ptrExit and delivers it on ptrSkip. EntryAtt can then settle upstream, while the hops between ptrSkip and ptrExit, starting with Skipped, never see their outgoing HTLC fulfilled and can at best be refunded. The rule emits Skipped(ptrSkip, x) but neither Redeemed nor FeeEarned. It yields the wormhole trace of Sec. V-E (Wormhole_Fee_Theft_Reachable), and the hop-bypass theorems (Sec. V-E, VI) show that, if the sender settles, a forwarder at positions 1 to 6 of the route, or at any position of a single-offer payment, is bypassed only if some key was compromised.

Rename to B. Verification Results and open the subsection with: Table I lists every verification run of our artifact, one per Makefile target; make all runs them in order. All results were obtained with Tamarin 1.10 (which reports the Maude version used, 3.2, as unsupported) and reproduced on a laptop with a 6 GB heap limit (MEM=6G).

notes.anchor: Our model includes the value of each HTLC
notes.html: Replace by (end of Sec. V-A2, after the Forward_HTLC paragraph): Amounts and fees are modelled per hop only. Forward_HTLC reads the incoming amount, the fee and the outgoing amount from the network (In(%vIn), In(%fee), In(%vOut), natural-number terms) and enforces Eq(%vIn, %vOut %+ %fee), so incoming = outgoing + fee holds at every hop by construction. The three values are kept in IntermediaryPending. Sender_Offer_HTLC, the invoice and the Route facts carry no amount, so amounts are not chained along the path, and the model makes no statement about end-to-end value, such as the amount the receiver obtains or the total fee the sender pays. We keep per-hop fees because the wormhole of Sec. V-E is a fee theft. The fee is a single per-hop quantity rather than Lightning's base_fee + fee_rate formula, and we prove nothing about fee policy.

notes.anchor: The wormhole is exactly the gap
notes.html: Replace by: In the wormhole trace, the bypassed honest hop emits FeeCharged but never FeeEarned, although the sender settles and the receiver is paid (Wormhole_Fee_Theft_Reachable, Sec. V-E). Conversely, a hop whose key is never compromised earns a fee only after it has forwarded the payment and its outgoing HTLC has been redeemed (Fee_Only_On_Successful_Forward).

Replace by: We deliberately leave out three things. First, channel capacity: Forward_HTLC has no Wallet premise and HTLCs do not change the balances in StateA and StateB, so a forward never fails for lack of funds. Second, concurrent HTLCs on one channel: Mutex(ptr) is taken when an HTLC is added to channel ptr and given back when that HTLC is redeemed or refunded, so a channel carries at most one pending HTLC at a time; later payments can reuse it, each with a payment hash not used on that channel before (Restr. OneHTLCPerHashPerChannel). Third, onion routing: the sender chooses only the first hop, each forwarder chooses its next hop among its own channels, and route information is kept in local state rather than sent in layered encryption. We therefore make no claims about hiding who pays whom, and the wormhole appears purely as fee theft, as also characterized in [6].

lightning.spthy is our main model. It contains the channel layer of Sec. V-A1, multi-hop routing with the single generic rule Forward_HTLC (Sec. V-A2) and the wormhole rule AttackerSkip, all under one Dolev-Yao adversary that can compromise long-term keys. In its default mode (make verify), all 55 lemmas are verified: 32 safety lemmas about channels and payments (Sec. V-C, V-D); 13 lemmas (six theorems and seven helpers) showing that the forwarders at positions 1 to 6 of a route cannot be bypassed unless some key was compromised (Sec. VI-A); and 10 exists-trace lemmas. These show that the model is not vacuous (channel updates, cooperative closes, refunds and honest multi-hop payments are reachable), that the assumptions of our safety lemmas matter (a payment without a matching invoice can settle once the receiver's key is compromised; a compromised intermediary can lose), and that the wormhole is reachable. make general runs the same file without the three liveness restrictions and proves the bypass theorem for routes of any length, Any_Hop_Skip_Requires_Compromise (Sec. VI); since removing restrictions only adds traces, this all-traces result also holds in the default mode. lightning_aux.spthy holds five small, self-contained models, one per flag: the PTLC countermeasure and its HTLC baseline (Sec. VI-E), two timing models (block clock, CLTV delta) that make explicit the deadlines the main model abstracts into untimed timeout events, and the early-timeout race, the trace pattern that Timeout_Race_Blocked excludes in the main model for uncompromised forwarders. make necessity removes one liveness restriction at a time (Sec. V-D).
